title: Allergy: mast cell mediators and the drugs that block them
ariaLabel: Schematic of an allergic reaction: allergen binds IgE on mast cells, which release histamine and leukotrienes. Anti-IgE antibodies and mast cell stabilisers reduce mast cell activation, H1 antihistamines block histamine receptors, and montelukast-type drugs block leukotriene receptors.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.

drugs.label: mast cell stabiliser or anti-IgE type

blockInfo: A drug of the chosen class acting at this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less passes here, with the effects shown at the cholesterol and the LDL receptors.

nodes.label: Allergen and IgE
nodes.info: Allergen binds IgE on the surface of mast cells.

nodes.label: Mediators released
nodes.info: Granules and lipid mediators released by the mast cell.

nodes.label: Histamine
nodes.info: Released from mast cell granules within minutes.

nodes.label: Histamine effect
nodes.info: Itch, sneezing, swelling and widened vessels.

nodes.label: Leukotrienes
nodes.info: Made by mast cells from arachidonic acid.

nodes.label: Leukotriene effect
nodes.info: Airway narrowing, mucus and nasal congestion.

nodes.label: Allergic symptoms
nodes.info: A teaching score for allergic symptoms, set by the allergen exposure and by the mediators that reach their receptors.

edges.label: mast cell trigger
edges.info: Mast cell stabilisers (cromolyn-type) reduce release of mediators; anti-IgE antibodies (omalizumab) remove IgE so allergen cannot trigger the cell.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: H1 receptors
edges.info: H1 antihistamines block histamine at its H1 receptor, easing itch, sneezing and running nose.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: CysLT1 receptors
edges.info: Leukotriene receptor antagonists (montelukast-type drugs) block CysLT1 receptors, helping airway swelling and nasal congestion.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

sources: Where each class acts. H1 antihistamines block histamine receptors, mast cell stabilisers and anti-IgE reduce mediator release, and leukotriene antagonists block CysLT1 receptors. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Adrenaline for anaphylaxis, corticosteroids, immunotherapy, H2 blockers, first and second generation differences, sedation and anticholinergic effects, asthma care and adverse effects are left out. Allergic symptoms are drawn as a teaching score. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
